questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of mitochondria?
questions.solution: Mitochondria possess their own circular DNA (mtDNA) which can replicate independently. mIDNA can produce its own $m$ RNA and protein and some of the enzymes required for functioning. They can produce new mitochondria by division or binary fission from pre-existing mitochondria. Mitochondria also have their own ribosomes but they are of 70 S type like that of prokaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is key event of anaphase of mitotic division?
options: Chromosomes are moved to spindle equator and get aligned through spindle fibres to both poles.
Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements.
questions.solution:
Chromosomes are moved to spindle equator and get aligned through spindle fibres to both poles in metaphase of mitotic cell division. Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements in telophase of mitotic cell
division. During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome divides and two chromatids separate completely to become daughter chromosomes. The daughter chromosomes move towards the opposite poles.

questions.solution: In the first meiotic division or heterotypic division, the reduction of chromosome number occurs resulting in the formation of two haploid cells. The second meiotic division is homotypic division.

questions.subject: Botany

Assertion : Net primary productivity is gross primary productivity minus respiration.
Reason : Secondary productivity is produced by heterotrophs.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Net primary productivity is the rate of organic matter built up or stored by producers in their bodies in a unit area/volume per unit time. Net productivity is equal to gross primary productivity minus loss due to respiration and other reasons. Rate of increase in energy containing organic matter or biomass by heterotrophs or consumers per unit time and area is known as secondary productivity.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a bioassay for cytokinins?
questions.solution: Cytokinins have the ability to retard the degradation of chlorophyll in excised leaves. Hence, chlorophyll preservation test is a bioassay for cytokinin. Dwarf maize test is a bioassay for gibberellins as they induce internodal growth in genetically dwarf varieties of plants like pea and maize.

questions.q: A series combination of resistor $(R)$ and capacitor $(C)$ is connected to an AC source of angular frequency $\omega$. Keeping the voltage same, if the frequency is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, the current becomes half of the original current. Then the ratio of the capacitive reactance and resistance at the former frequency is
questions.solution:
In the first case, capacitive reactance,
$X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}$
Impedance of the circuit, $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit, $I=\frac{V}{Z}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}} \ldots$ (i)
In the second case, $\omega^{\prime}=\frac{\omega}{3}\therefore \quad$ Capacitive reactance,
$X_C^{\prime}=\frac{1}{\omega^{\prime} C}=\frac{1}{\frac{\omega}{3} C}=\frac{3}{\omega C}=3 X_C$
Impedance of the circuit,
$Z^{\prime}=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^{\prime 2}}=\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit,
$\frac{I}{2}=\frac{V}{Z^{\prime}}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}}$
Divide (ii) by (i), we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}=\frac{R^2+X_C^2}{R^2+9 X_C^2} \\ & 5 X_C^2=3 R^2 \text { or } \frac{X_C}{R}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}=\sqrt{0.6}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A body of mass $m_1$ collides elastically with another body of mass $m_2$ at rest. If the velocity of $m_1$ after collision becomes $2 / 3$ times its initial velocity, the ratio of their masses is
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be the initial velocity of body of mass $m_1$ before collision. Since collision is elastic both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. $\therefore m_1 v=m_1 \frac{2}{3} v+m_2 v_2$ or $m_1\left(v-\frac{2}{3} v\right)=m_2 v_2$
Also, $\frac{1}{2} m_1 v^2=\frac{1}{2} m_1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 v^2+\frac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2$ or $m_1\left(v^2-\frac{4}{9} v^2\right)=m_2 v_2^2$ or $\frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}$ Equating (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{aligned} & \frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}=\frac{3 v_2}{v} \text { or } \frac{v_2}{v}=\frac{5}{3} \\ & \therefore \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{3 \times 5}{3}=\frac{5}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: Allergy is an exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment. Anti-histamine, adrenaline and steroids quickly reduce the symptoms of allergy that include sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing.

Ventral respiratory group is located in the ventrolateral part of the medulla oblongata which can cause either inspiration or expiration depending upon the neurons stimulated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The ventilation movements of the lungs in mammals are governed by
questions.solution: Ventilation is the movement of air through the conducting passages between the atmosphere and the lungs. The air moves through the passage because of pressure gradients that are produced by contraction and relaxation of diaphragm and intercostal muscles during inspiration and expiration.

questions.q: Conn's disease is caused by the oversecretion of
questions.solution: Conn's disease is caused by over secretion of aldosterone from adrenal gland. This overproduction leads to the retention of sodium and loss of potassium in the body, resulting in high blood pressure. Other symptoms may occur because high aldosterone levels in the blood act on the kidney.

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.

questions.solution: Auerbach's plexus is a network of nerve cell and parasympathetic nerve fibre present in the muscularis layer of wall of alimentary canal. It controls peristalsis. On the other hand, Meissner's plexus is a network of nerve cells and sympathetic nerve fibre present in the submucosa layer of wall of alimentary canal. It controls the secretion of intestinal juice.

questions.q: It is a disease which mainly affects mucous membrane of urinogenital tract. In males, burning feeling on passing urine, after a yellow discharge occurs, that is accompanied by fever, headache and feeling of illness. Its name is
questions.solution: Gonorrhoea is caused by a bacterium, Neisseria gonorrhoeae. It spreads through sexual contact, common toilets and underclothes. Gonorrhoea affects both male and female genitals. The bacterium lives in genital tubes, produces pus-containing discharge, pain around genitalia and burning sensation during urination. It damages the eyes of babies born to infected mothers.

options: Erection will be able to occur, but ejaculation will not be possible.

Reason : Appetency is also called doctrine of desire.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: According to Lamarck, a change in environment brings about changes in organisms. It gives rise to new needs. New needs or desires produce new structures and change habits of the organisms. Doctrine of desire is called appetency. It can be shown by the following example- Water birds (duck etc.) developed their webbed feet by constant stretching of digits and the skin between them for skimming the water surface and for swimming. The transmission of acquired characters is the most important principle usually termed as the Lamarckian doctrine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: At a particular locus, frequency of allele ' $A$ ' is 0.6 and that of allele ' $a$ ' is 0.4 . What would be the frequency of heterozygotes in a random mating population at equilibrium?
questions.solution:
In a stable population, for a gene with two alleles, ' $A$ ' (dominant) and 'a' (recessive), if the frequency of ' $A$ ' is $p$ and the frequency of ' $\mathrm{a}$ ' is $q$, then the frequencies of the three possible genotypes (AA, Aa and aa) can be expressed by the Hardy-Weinberg equation:
$p^2+2 p q+q^2=1$
where $p^2=$ Frequency of AA (homozygous dominant) individuals
$q^2=$ Frequency of aa (homozygous recessive) individuals
$2 p q=$ Frequency of Aa (heterozygous) individuals.
So, $p=0.6$ and $q=0.4$ (given)
$\begin{aligned} \therefore 2 p q(\text { frequency of heterozygote }) & =2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 \\ & =0.48 .\end{aligned}$

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.

questions.solution: Ectotherms or cold-blooded animals, cannot regulate their body temperature and are unable to maintain a constant internal temperature. Their body temperature tends to match with the environmental temperature in which they live, (e.g., frogs and snakes). These animals are not able to remain active under cold conditions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : Mullerian and Batesian mimicry both are protective mimicry.
Reason : Viceroy butterfly shows Mullerian mimicry.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Defensive or protective mimicry takes place when organisms are able to avoid harmful encounters by deceiving enemies into treating them as something else. In Batesian mimicry, a harmless species poses as harmful to deceive predator. In Mullerian mimicry, two or more harmful species mutually advertise themselves as harmful for their mutual benifit. Viceroy butterfly mimics unpalatable toxic Monarch butterfly, thus, shows Batesian mimicry.

questions.solution: Diseases or infections which are transmitted through sexual intercourse are called sexually transmitted diseases (STDs). AIDS and hepatitis-B are sexually transmitted diseases. Hepatitis-B and AIDS can also be transmitted by sharing of contaminated syringes, surgical instruments with infected persons, transfusion of blood, etc. There is no permanent cure for AIDS and hepatitis-B.

questions.q: The kind of epithelium present in inner surface of bronchioles and Fallopian tubes is
questions.solution: The inner surface of bronchioles and Fallopian tubes possess ciliated epithelium. In the respiratory tract cilia help to push mucus towards the pharynx. In Fallopian tube, the cilia help to move an egg towards the uterus.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is the first formed tissue in the embryo?
questions.solution: Epithelial tissue is formed first in the embryo. The epithelial tissue arises from all the three primary germ layers of the embryo - ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
